answers.answer: Build top to bottom from 1 randomly dealt Conflict I, then 5 randomly dealt Conflict II, then all 4 Conflict III in shuffled order. Shuffle each tier first; return unused cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: final order from top to bottom; return unused Conflict cards without looking.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on the Leader and a third Swordmaster Agent beside the board; 3 troops in garrison and 9 in supply; 1 water; one cube at bottom of each of four Influence tracks (0 Influence); VP is 0 in three-player and 1 in four-player.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 5–8: two Agents, third Agent; 3 troops in garrison; 1 water; score 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal early. After Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, including Agent turns; Plot Intrigue can only be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns, so not later in the phase.
answers.evidence: Once you have taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped; Plot cards during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one hand card with a matching Agent icon and choose one icon to send one Agent to an unoccupied space. The card must have an Agent icon; pay entry costs and meet requirements immediately before resolving effects. A card cannot send multiple Agents.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: play one card; choose only one Agent icon; space must be unoccupied; costs paid immediately before effects.

answers.answer: No. Entry costs are paid before card or space effects, so 3 spice is insufficient for Conspire’s 4-spice cost. Once entry is legal and paid, resolve board-space effect, Agent box, and Faction Influence in any order.
answers.evidence: Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects; effects ... in any order, after paying entry cost.

answers.answer: You may deploy the 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 more from the garrison, for a maximum of 5; the four already there do not raise that limit. Undeployed recruits remain in the garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits normally go to garrison.
answers.evidence: Combat space deployment: any or all troops recruited this turn plus up to two more; Rally Troops table effect and non-Combat-space rule.

answers.answer: Reveal all remaining hand cards; resolve their Reveal boxes in any order (only cards revealed now, not Agent-played cards); set Combat strength; Clean Up all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns into discard.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn four steps; Clean Up puts all cards in front of you into discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, the Imperium Row refills immediately and you may acquire its replacement if affordable. Persuasion can be pooled across sources and split across cards. Leftover Persuasion is lost; acquired cards go to discard and cannot be used right away. Acquire-box effects occur once when acquired.
answers.evidence: Row must always have five cards; may acquire replacement; pool/split Persuasion; never saved; acquired cards go to discard; Acquire effect at acquisition.

answers.answer: 3 troops plus 4 swords gives 10 strength (2 per troop, 1 per sword). If the last troop is removed, strength is 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords. Over 20, flip Combat marker to +20 and start again at beginning of track.
answers.evidence: Each troop ... 2 strength; each sword ... 1; no troop means 0; over 20 flip marker.

answers.answer: Players with at least one Conflict troop may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass, starting with First Player and clockwise. Passing earlier does not bar later play. Resolve after all involved players pass consecutively. Win-trigger cards are played after winning, before next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: starting with First Player; may play any number or pass; not required to pass just because passed earlier; win cards after win.

answers.answer: A and B tied first means neither wins and each gets the second reward; C and D then compete for third, with C receiving it (four-player game). A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, even in 2- or 3-player games; tie for third gets nothing; 0 strength gets nothing. After rewards troops return to supply.
answers.evidence: Tied first: no one wins, tied players second reward; remaining players compete third. Tied second gets third; tied third nothing; troops to supply.

answers.answer: In Phase 4 Makers, add 1 bonus spice from bank to each unoccupied Maker space among Great Flat, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin. Normal harvesting happens when an Agent visits a space: Imperial Basin 1 base spice, Hagga 2, Great Flat 3, plus accumulated bonus. If an Agent moves away and the space is empty in Makers, bonus spice accumulates.
answers.evidence: Makers checks three named spaces; if no Agent, place 1 spice. Maker spaces edge case says bonus accumulates if still empty.

answers.answer: The 10-VP check happens at end of round in Recall, not mid-round; an empty Conflict Deck also triggers end then. Resolve Endgame Intrigue cards before declaring most-VP winner. Ties break by spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then most recent Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Game end trigger at Phase 5; Endgame cards first; full tiebreak list including most recently took Reveal turn.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence gain 1 VP, lost below 2 and regained upon returning to 2. At 4, gain the track bonus and keep it if dropping below; it may be earned again by re-advancing. First to 4 takes Alliance; an opponent advancing to a higher space takes it. Tying the holder does not; if holder loses Influence while tied, a previously tied player takes it.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence and Alliances sections describe VP, retained/re-earned bonus, first to 4, higher-space transfer, and tied-holder rule.

answers.answer: If you lose 1 while tied at 5 with two opponents, one of the previously tied players takes the Alliance; you choose which if several were tied. If you were sole player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the token; if nobody else has 4+, return it to the board.
answers.evidence: If holder loses Influence while previously tied ... if several were tied, holder chooses; holder loses token falling to 3 or less.

answers.answer: Discard means a card from hand unless stated otherwise; it goes to discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from hand, discard, or in play to box; Reserve cards return to Reserve. Trashing is optional except paying a cost or when directed to trash itself. Do not reshuffle early to inspect an empty deck’s top card.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards; Deck exhaustion: can't reshuffle early, e.g. top-card inspection of empty deck.

answers.answer: A controller gets 1 Solari whenever anyone visits Arrakeen or Carthag, or 1 spice for Imperial Basin. Winning a matching Conflict places your Control marker on its flag, replacing an opponent’s. When a matching Conflict is revealed later, you may deploy one troop from supply to Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control section: visit bonuses; marker replaces opponent; defensive bonus on matching Conflict reveal.

answers.answer: Use unused color, put its cube at bottom of each Influence track, remaining cubes in supply, no troops in garrison; remove three 1P Arrakeen cards, shuffle remaining Hagal deck, place deck and three Agents near supply. Hagal acts after each First Player Agent turn if it has an Agent. It never Reveals, gets no resources, VP, or Conflict rewards, but may hold Alliances.
answers.evidence: Two-player setup and overview: three Agents; no troops in garrison; turn schedule; never Reveal; cannot score VP/earn rewards, can take Alliances.

answers.answer: If indicated space is occupied, reveal another card until eligible. Reshuffle immediately if deck empty or Reshuffle appears; continue revealing. Ignore space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve card icons/instructions. Troop icons recruit, deploying on Combat spaces, otherwise garrison; every Combat visit automatically deploys up to two garrison troops (one if only one). Harvest Spice takes Maker space with most bonus, tie by total base-plus-bonus; if none has bonus, reveal another card. For a two-space card, use only condition-matching option; if occupied, draw again, never switch options.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns paragraphs specify all listed procedures.

answers.answer: If Hagal has a Conflict troop, at start of Combat reveal Hagal cards until non-Reshuffle; add that card’s swords to 2 per deployed troop, then humans may play Combat Intrigue. Hagal occupies its rank but gets no reward. If it wins a space a human controls, remove that Control marker and Hagal does not replace it. Human tie for second earns third reward; ordinary third earns none.
answers.evidence: Combat strength procedure; Hagal receives no reward but occupies rank; control and tie rules.

answers.answer: Round Start reveals the top Conflict card and each player draws 5. In non-ending Recall, return Mentat to its space if needed, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player marker clockwise, then start next round. Sort Through the Chaos winner takes Mentat at start of next round.
answers.evidence: Phase 1; Phase 5 Recall; official FAQ timing for Mentat reward.

answers.answer: Bank resources are not limited; substitute if tokens run out. If your troop supply is out, you cannot recruit more until troops return.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources are not limited, substitute; Recruiting: if supply is out, cannot recruit.

answers.answer: Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns. Other Leader abilities operate as described on the Leader. Cards of any type can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Overview: Leader abilities and Signet Ring; cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr is a City-icon space, requires 2+ Fremen Influence, recruits a troop and gains 1 water; it is a Combat space, so deployment is allowed. At 1 Influence you cannot enter, so cannot use a card effect to reach 2 after entry.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table and Combat spaces list; must pay/meet requirements before resolving effects.

answers.answer: Combat spaces: Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station, Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, Great Flat, Heighliner, Hardy Warriors, Stillsuits. Research Station and Great Flat are included; Conspire is not.
answers.evidence: Complete list of Combat spaces; other spaces including Conspire do not normally allow deployment.

answers.answer: Wealth: Emperor, no cost, +1 Emperor Influence and 2 Solari. Conspire: Emperor, 4 spice, +1 Emperor Influence, 5 Solari, recruit 2, draw Intrigue. Foldspace: Guild, no cost, +1 Guild Influence, acquire Foldspace. Heighliner: Guild, 6 spice, +1 Guild Influence, recruit 5 and gain 2 water. Secrets: Bene Gesserit, no cost, +1 Influence, draw Intrigue and each opponent with 4+ Intrigue gives one randomly selected. Selective Breeding: Bene Gesserit, 2 spice, +1 Influence, trash one card to draw two. Stillsuits: Fremen, no cost, +1 Influence and 1 water. Hardy Warriors: Fremen, 1 water, +1 Influence, recruit 2.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists costs/effects and Faction Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City, no cost, recruit 1 and draw a card; controller gets 1 Solari. Carthag: City, no cost, recruit 1 and draw Intrigue; controller gets 1 Solari. Research Station: City, 2 water, draw 3 cards. Secure Contract: Spice Trade, no cost, 3 Solari. Imperial Basin: Spice Trade, no cost, 1 spice plus bonus spice; controller gets 1 spice. Hagga Basin: Spice Trade, 1 water, 2 spice plus bonus. Great Flat: Spice Trade, 2 water, 3 spice plus bonus.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table.

answers.answer: Sell Melange is a Spice Trade space: pay 2/3/4/5 spice for 6/8/10/12 Solari, respectively; one exchange per turn.
answers.evidence: Sell Melange table row gives rates and one exchange per turn; board-space category list places it in Spice Trade.

answers.answer: High Council costs 5 Solari, once per game, and places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat; benefit (2 Persuasion) begins each Reveal turn thereafter. Swordmaster costs 8 Solari, once per game, and gives the third Agent placed on Leader; you have three Agents for the rest of game, including this round.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table and Special Rules: Swordmaster & High Council.

answers.answer: Hall of Oratory has no cost, recruits one troop and grants 1 Persuasion during your Reveal if you have an Agent there. Rally Troops costs 4 Solari and recruits 4 troops to garrison. Mentat costs 2 Solari, draws a card, and if Mentat is there lets you take it as an Agent this round; return in Recall.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table.

answers.answer: Yes. Return recalled Agent to your Leader; you may use it on another Agent turn in the same round. It does not reopen turns after you have Revealed.
answers.evidence: Recall effects special rule.

answers.answer: Fremen Bond works with at least one other Fremen card in play, including an Agent-played card and a card revealed this turn. Those cards remain in play until Clean Up unless trashed; two Bond cards activate each other regardless of order.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond rule.

answers.answer: A single gain-two-Influence effect cannot be split between Factions. Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance; numeric Influence icon requires at least shown Influence with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons rule.

answers.answer: Intrigue cards are kept face down, separate from deck; may look at them, reveal only when played, and resolved cards go face up beside Intrigue Deck. Plot is played on own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat only during Combat; Endgame at game end. If deck empties, shuffle discards into a new deck. Intrigue costs/conditions must be met to play.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section; optional arrow paragraph says Intrigue costs and conditions must be met.

answers.answer: Yes. A delayed Plot such as Charisma or Recruitment Mission can be played during an Agent turn; leave it face up until next Reveal turn, use it then, and discard it.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards delayed Plot paragraph.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal must immediately be revealed and used that turn; it cannot become an Agent turn. A card drawn after Reveal stays in hand for next round, when you still draw five additional cards.
answers.evidence: Reveal effects card-draw rule.

answers.answer: Most effects are mandatory unless they say may, are optional arrows, or optional black-X trash. Optional arrow payment/effect can be declined on ordinary cards; entry costs are required, and Intrigue costs/conditions must be met. Standalone black-X trash optional; trashing to pay a cost required; non-arrow instruction to trash itself mandatory. An optional arrow effect may be done once, never repeated by paying again.
answers.evidence: Agent turn optional effects and arrow rules.

answers.answer: Play Bindu Suspension at start of Agent turn, before anything else; draw a card, then immediately end turn.
answers.evidence: Rulebook clarification: Bindu Suspension.

answers.answer: Calculated Hire can take Mentat only from its starting Landsraad position, not another player or another space. Sort Through the Chaos winner takes it at start of next round and uses it that round.
answers.evidence: Calculated Hire and Mentat reward clarifications.

answers.answer: Kwisatz Haderach permits an Agent turn with no unused Agents by sending an Agent already on a board space, even to same space. It cannot reuse High Council or Swordmaster and cannot overcome The Voice.
answers.evidence: Kwisatz Haderach clarification.

answers.answer: The Voice marker is removed on your next turn and prevents opponents, including via Kwisatz Haderach, from sending Agents to that space for one turn. Mark it with an available Control marker.
answers.evidence: The Voice clarification.

answers.answer: Affected opponents choose their own cards to discard from their hands, in order starting with your left and clockwise. Test of Humanity requires a possible choice: no discard from an empty hand and no losing a deployed troop they do not have.
answers.evidence: Opponent discards clarification.

answers.answer: After setup and before first round, secretly choose two of four Baron tokens and place them Faction-side down on Leader; return other two unseen. Reveal later for reward, only once per game.
answers.evidence: Baron Vladimir Harkonnen clarification.

answers.answer: Yes, Demand Respect may be funded with spice taken first from a Conflict reward, and To the Victor… can likewise fund it. A win-trigger Intrigue drawn as a victory reward may be played immediately. No win-trigger card can be played on a first-place tie because nobody won.
answers.evidence: Demand Respect and Combat tie clarifications.

answers.answer: Yes, zero is allowed when an effect says retreat any number. Retreated troops move from Conflict to garrison; lost troops return to supply.
answers.evidence: Losing vs. retreating troops rule.

answers.answer: Assassination Mission does not trash itself for 4 Solari; another effect must trash it. Imperial Spy draws Intrigue only with its own self-trash effect, not when another effect trashes it.
answers.evidence: Assassination Mission / Imperial Spy clarification.

answers.answer: Yes, keep VP from acquiring The Spice Must Flow even if later trashed. Guild Bankers discount applies to each copy acquired that turn.
answers.evidence: The Spice Must Flow / Guild Bankers clarification.

answers.answer: Count The Spice Must Flow in your deck and discard pile. First condition: at least two copies gives 1 VP. Second: have more than each opponent gives separate 1 VP; compare opponents individually, and any opponent with at least as many means this condition fails. Either condition can score alone.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification.

answers.answer: Ruthless Negotiator triggers only for printed Solari cost of a board space, not a card ability costing Solari. Ariana’s Spice Addict is mandatory and applies only to spice harvested by sending an Agent to Maker space, not other spice gains.
answers.evidence: Count Ilban / Ariana clarification.

answers.answer: Base spice is 1 Imperial Basin, 2 Hagga Basin, 3 Great Flat; accumulated bonus is not base. Liet Kynes counts qualifying cards from Agent turns this round and current Reveal turn, gaining 2 Persuasion each.
answers.evidence: Carryall / Liet Kynes clarification.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire set-aside card. You may acquire it by another effect, but the 1-Persuasion discount does not apply then. If not acquired by end of your next Reveal, remove it from game.
answers.evidence: Helena Richese — Manipulate clarification.

answers.answer: Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in Conflict but not a troop in your own supply. Gun Thopter’s Agent box does not affect an opponent with no garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Double Cross / Gun Thopter clarification.

answers.answer: Shifting Allegiances may lose and gain Influence with same Faction for net +1, but must actually pay the loss; a Faction at zero cannot pay. Tracks have six spaces; 3 Influence is immediately above the 2-Influence VP space.
answers.evidence: Shifting Allegiances clarification; Faction Influence rule.

answers.answer: Recruitment Mission’s destination choice applies only to Reveal-turn acquisitions that round, not Agent-turn acquisitions. During Reveal, choose independently for each card whether it goes atop deck or to discard.
answers.evidence: Recruitment Mission clarification.

answers.answer: Refocus reshuffles your deck if discard pile is empty. Any cards drawn during Reveal must immediately be revealed and used that turn.
answers.evidence: Refocus / Poison Snooper clarification.

answers.answer: Missionaria Protectiva is Bene Gesserit; include only two copies in Imperium deck after replacing misprints.
answers.evidence: Missionaria Protectiva erratum.

answers.answer: Yes. You can score above 12 VP; printed Score track end is not a limit.
answers.evidence: Tiebreakers paragraph: score above 12 VP.

answers.answer: Rivals are affected by effects targeting opponents or players if they have the specified resources. Hagal gets no Influence-track bonuses; Signet Ring icons have no effect in two-player play.
answers.evidence: House Hagal overview and Agent turn rules.

answers.answer: Hagal acts after each First Player Agent turn only; not after second human’s turns or after a Reveal. Swordmaster can let first player take a third Agent turn, so Hagal may take three turns instead of two; actual count follows First Player’s Agent turns and available Hagal Agents, max three.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns paragraph.

answers.answer: Ordinary Persuasion cannot buy Foldspace; it requires an acquire-Foldspace icon, normally from Foldspace board space.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: Foldspace requires acquire-Foldspace icon and cannot be bought with Persuasion.

answers.answer: City remains; Dispatch adds missing Faction icons only and does not duplicate existing icons, so no second Fremen icon.
answers.evidence: Dispatch an Envoy clarification.

answers.answer: Yes, troops recruited this turn from any source, including Plot Intrigue, can deploy with space/card recruits when Agent goes to Combat space. You may add up to two more garrison troops, but cannot re-recruit them to evade that limit.
answers.evidence: Deploying rule: recruits this turn from any source plus up to two garrison; cannot re-recruit garrison troops.

answers.answer: Draw the one card remaining, then reshuffle discard to form new deck and continue drawing two. Cards still face up in play are not in discard and do not enter the shuffle; Clean Up sends them to discard later.
answers.evidence: Deck exhaustion: when unable to draw, reshuffle discard and continue; cards in play go to discard at Clean Up.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s standard 10-card starting deck and place face down left of Leader. Shuffle Imperium deck face down and deal 5 face up; shuffle Intrigue deck face down. Put Arrakis Liaison, Spice Must Flow, Foldspace in separate Reserve stacks beside Row. Place Mentat on its side in Mentat space and Alliance tokens on marked track areas. Choose initial First Player randomly and give them marker before Round 1.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, 5, 9.

answers.answer: Unused player components are kept in supply in clear view of all players. Intrigue cards remain face down and separate; their faces are not public, though their owner may look at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: remaining components in clear view; Intrigue cards kept face down, owner may look.

answers.answer: You may spend Persuasion to acquire before, between, or after Reveal effects; you need not finish all effects first.
answers.evidence: Reveal effects step explicitly says acquire before, between, or after effects.

answers.answer: City icon: Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station. Landsraad: High Council, Swordmaster, Hall of Oratory, Rally Troops, Mentat. Spice Trade: Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, Great Flat, Secure Contract, Sell Melange.
answers.evidence: Actions: board spaces category lists.

answers.answer: Phase 2 starts with First Player marker holder, then clockwise, taking one turn at a time. Each turn is Agent or Reveal; players generally Agent until out, but may Reveal early. Once Revealed, skipped for rest of phase; phase ends when all have Revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns description.

answers.answer: In three-player game, 8 strength wins top reward, 6 gets second, and 4 gets no reward for ordinary third. In four-player games ordinary third-place finisher gets third reward.
answers.evidence: Combat rewards: highest, second, 4-player ordinary third; two- and three-player third tie exception distinct.

answers.answer: At start of Combat, Hagal with at least one Conflict troop reveals a card in turn order; if Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again until combat card, then humans may play Combat Intrigue. No troop means no Hagal combat-bonus reveal.
answers.evidence: Combat strength procedure: if at least one troop, reveal; then humans play cards.

answers.answer: First condition is having at least two Spice Must Flow cards, worth 1 VP. Separate second condition is having more than each opponent, worth 1 VP. Each scores independently, so either alone gives 1 VP and both give 2.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification.

answers.answer: Yes. Sardaukar Legion’s Reveal box deploys up to 3 troops from your garrison during Reveal effects, before Set Strength; those troops then count toward strength.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn example: Sardaukar Legion deploys up to three from garrison during Reveal effects before Set Strength.

answers.answer: Landsraad Popularity discounts by 1 Solari the entry cost of a Landsraad (green) space when Leto sends Agent; apply before paying. Prudent Diplomacy optionally pays 1 spice for 1 Influence with a Faction where an opponent has more Influence than Leto; cannot target if no opponent is ahead.
answers.evidence: Duke Leto Atreides FAQ clarification.

answers.answer: Harvest Spice chooses Maker space with most bonus spice; tie breaks by total spice (base plus bonus). If none has bonus, reveal another Hagal card. Harvested bonus spice is removed and returned to bank; Hagal accumulates no resources.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Harvest Spice rule.

answers.answer: Choose two different Faction gain-one icons and gain 1 Influence with each; cannot put both in one Faction. This differs from one generic gain-two icon, which also cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons: Machinations Choose two means choose two different Factions.

answers.answer: Choose one Master Tactician option: 3 swords OR retreat up to 3 troops. If retreating, move troops from Conflict to your garrison; you do not also get swords.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards: OR chooses one effect; Master Tactician example; retreat rule.
